mission.title: Death in Many Forms
mission.description: Hunt down the Apothecary, the kill-code specialist working for the Merovingian.

npc.say:
The "Morpheus" signal tracked so avidly by the adherents of Zion experienced a glitch in its last broadcast, according to reports.
Remember that the System confirmed the terrorist Morpheus as terminated by the Assassin program some time ago, operative.

You should spend every available moment training, {player}. Although perfection is not possible, there is no excuse for not operating with the highest possible efficiency in the System's service. I did not always understand this myself... Fortunately, I have realized my error, and I am happy to report a significant increase in my simulated combat rating.
You are one of our more effective operatives, {player}. I just felt I should mention that.
Aberrant behavior by a System program should always be reported immediately. In almost all cases, repairs can be effected within a very short period. It is our duty to maximize program uptime.

phase.briefing:
It appears, operative, that rapid action against the Merovingian is necessary to deter him from making the mistake of further escalating hostilities against the System.
The kill-code specialist he removed from our mainframes, the Apothecary, is to be deleted. This is the second time she has entered the Matrix without our permission; our indulgence is at an end.
Laboratory facilities where the Merovingian is believed to be employing the Apothecary have been uncovered. Search the area for any sign of the Apothecary, and eliminate all resistance.

enter.say: It looks like the Machines already got some units in there. I'm seeing Machine and Exile signals on my screen--can't tell if one of them's the Apothecary or not.
Geez... Our guys are droppin' like flies in there.

talk.say: Hey, there's one of the good guys. They're already making progress there, then.
I have detected a program in the vicinity that I believe to be the Apothecary. She is-- Zrrk!

done.say: "She is zrrk"? What does that... Oh. Um... Okay, an Agent just spontaneously fell over dead. This probably isn't good.
One of those signals is moving away from you now... Right through that next door. Hurry!
That isn't the one! Keep going!
Aw, what th--? It just blipped off my screen. They must have ported her out somehow. Great. I hope Gray has some other lead.

phase.briefing:
We are continuing to track the signal on wide area scans, operative. It matches the last confirmed Matrix RSI profile of the Apothecary; it also appears to employ her traditional "coup de grace," as she has termed it.
Ah, I see an explanation is necessary. The Apothecary possesses a routine allowing her to cause a lower-level RSI's function to cease with only a movement of her hand. While this does not usually result in permanent deletion, it is somewhat inconvenient when used against our resources.
Hm... The scan readings suggest that the Merovingians are mustering their forces. Proceed to the indicated location, and procure backup programs from Agent Pace. You will be pleased to see her fully operational again, I am sure.

enter.say: I knew she'd bounce back! That's my Pace! Looks like she's in there with some assault programs for you.

talk.say:
Ah... Greetings, {player}. Yes, thank you; I am feeling very well.
Ohh! I wish I could go with you... But, ah, that is not my assigned task. Take these programs then, {player}, and eliminate the Merovingian's forces!

done.say: Wow, she's kind of feisty after being out of action for a while, isn't she?

Terminate the System's enemies!
I will follow your progress with great interest, tesoro.
The Apothecary is an exceedingly dangerous program.
We should proceed, {player}. Other Machine elements are already moving into attack positions around the target.

objective.text: Lead the Mechanics out of the area

phase.briefing: Our forces are converging at the target's location, operative. It appears to be a manufacturing facility, possibly related to the Apothecary's kill-code work. Any evidence of such should be confiscated. However, your primary task is the deletion of the Apothecary herself. Remember that she is highly dangerous.

enter.say: I've got Machine and Exile signals all over the place in there. It's gonna be a brawl, no question.

Elite goggle-boys, eh? Looks like the Merv and the General are having some fun tag-teaming us.
Hey! Got that signal, close by. It's moving again!

done.say:
Blast.
Very well. Complete elimination of hostiles in that facility. You will then report to me.
There was a hefty chunk of unusual code on the Exile that just went down. Check them out.

objective.text: Get the code from the Exile Courier's body

done.say: Aha! I think I know what that is, and it if is, then we'd better get it to Gray, fast.

complete.say: Hostiles have been eliminated, {player}, although the primary target eluded our units.
We have survived to serve the System another day.

phase.briefing: Bring me the item you found immediately, operative.

enter.say: Gray's in there, and hey, there's Pace, too! Man, this is a red-letter day in my book. Okay, so the Apothecary got away... Eh, well, there's only so many Exiles we can be expected to delete in a single day, right?

objective.text: Give the code to Agent Gray

done.say:
Hm... Yes, this appears to be a portion of one of the stolen cheat codes. We know that the Merovingian located one recently; the presence of this at the Apothecary's workplace can be no coincidence. If her work for the Merovingian is not yet complete, the confiscation of this cheat code could retard their scheme significantly.
Her escape through the General's network terminal, however, serves as a setback to our own offensive against Merovingian and commando forces. We must make the permanent shutdown of the General's network our primary task.

complete.say:
The simulation's weather system is nearing a state of terminal malfunction; should this happen, bluepill casualties will begin to mount rapidly. Our own analysis has concluded that the most efficient way to achieve Sati's return, and the consequence restoration of weather control, lies in neutralizing her captor, the General.
The Oracle and Seraph, on the other hand, have, in association with Zion, been pursuing Sati directly. As expected, they do not appear to have made significant progress. I attempted to inform Seraph of the inutility of his tactics. He was...fairly unreceptive. It is possible that side effects of his recent accident continue to impair his logic functions.

It was very exciting to monitor your progress at the Merovingian's facility, tesoro. Do not blame yourself too much for failing to terminate the Apothecary on this occasion. I only regret that I was not permitted to assist in the attack personally; I feel confident that I could have helped prevent the traitor's escape.
Man, she's really gung-ho today! It's cute how she wants to help out. Maybe Gray should cut her a break. I can think of some assignments we could use her on...

mission.finish:
We must consider that the rumors of the Merovingian's attempted manufacture of a kill-code to use against the Oracle are likely to be accurate; there is no other plausible explanation for the close spatial and temporal proximity of the Apothecary, a cheat code, and code derived from the Oracle's own, found in the recent attack made by the Merovingian on Agent Pace.
While the Oracle's preservation is not in itself a primary goal, she serves an important role in certain systems that aid the stability of the simulation, such as her tutorship of Sati. We must also recognize that, given the current hostile climate, any action counter to those of the Merovingian and the General will tend to benefit the System. For these and other reasons, the deletion of the Apothecary has been given a high priority.
